name: Antijuan Wilkes Jr.
strengths: Wilkes gets immediate depth on the kickslide and uses length to keep speed rushers at arm's length while staying square.
Wilkes climbs to the second level cleanly on pulls — seals the off-ball LB with real lateral agility for a 6-5 tackle.
Wilkes strikes with hands inside the framework and resets without lunging when the rusher counters.
weaknesses: Wilkes still gets walked back on straight bull rush — hips rise under power and he needs more functional mass to anchor.
comparison: Wilkes comps to Kelvin Banks Jr. — 6-4/6-5 tackle mold with elite length and foot quickness who wins with kickslide depth and second-level mobility before the mass fully arrives.
projection: Wilkes projects as a Year 2–3 SEC starter at tackle (develop Year 1). Ceiling: multi-year SEC left tackle — the long Cass Tech tackle who sets the edge and climbs.
schemeFit: Wilkes fits a zone/gap hybrid tackle who can kickslide with length and still get to the second level in the run game.
staffNotes: Vault film desk verified 2026-08-10 from On3 Hudl sophomore embed. Comp size-matched within ~1–2" — not a Florida-alum default.
recruitingStory: Antijuan Wilkes Jr. is a 4-star OT · listed 6-5 / 265 · Cass Technical (Detroit, MI) · Natl #16 · Pos #2 · State #1 — Florida offered April; campus visit still pending (Vandy home + Missouri road planned).
angle: Lead with Cass Tech LT length + kickslide; Florida needs him on campus to convert the priority.
insiderNotes: Wilkes is a high-upside LT with elite length, nimble feet, and clean second-level movement. Anchor vs power is the growth item as he adds mass. Florida priority with campus still the next test.
